transcript.content: Hello, and welcome. I'm Dr. [Name], a psychiatrist. What brings you in to see me today?

My mom brought me. I... I don't know. I just... I can't really do anything lately. I just sit in my room mostly. I don't change my clothes or... I don't knit or journal or walk anymore. When my mom asks why, I just... I don't have the energy to even answer her.
How long have you been feeling this way — this lack of energy and not being able to do the things you normally do?
Um... a while. I guess... since I started community college. That was like... two years ago. Maybe two years and two months. I don't really remember.
Before you started community college two years ago, were you feeling okay — like your normal self — or had you been struggling with low mood and lack of energy before that?
I don't... I'm not really sure. I guess I was okay. I just... I don't really remember it that well.
In the two years before you started community college, do you remember having any periods where you felt really sad or depressed, or was your mood pretty stable back then?
I don't think so. I mean... I don't really know. It's just hard to remember back then. I guess... I guess it was stable. I didn't feel like this.
Before you started community college two years ago, did you ever have a time in your life — even if it was years earlier — when you felt depressed or very sad for weeks or months at a time?
No... I don't think so. I don't remember ever feeling sad for that long back then. It was just... I don't know. Just normal, I guess.

Since you started community college two years ago and started feeling this way, have there been any times when you felt better — like your mood lifted or you had more energy — even if it was just for a few weeks or a month?
No... I don't think so. It just kind of... stayed like this. I haven't really felt any different.
Looking back even further — to when you were younger, like in high school or earlier — did you ever have a time when you felt depressed or really down for a few weeks or more, even if it was brief?
Not really... I was just going to school. I didn't... I didn't have problems like that back then.

I want to make sure I understand your history correctly. Before you started community college two years ago, did you ever have a time — even just a week or two — when you felt noticeably sad, empty, or depressed, or when you lost interest in things you normally enjoyed?
No... I really didn't. I just... I don't remember feeling like that before college. Everything was just... regular, I guess. I didn't have those problems.
Have you ever had a time — even just for a few days or a week — when you felt really energized, like you needed much less sleep than usual, or when your mood felt unusually good or high?
No... I don't think so. I just... I sleep. I've never really felt energized or... high like that.

During these two years since you started college, has there been any time — even just a week or two — when you felt a bit better, had more energy, or felt more like yourself, before it went back to how it is now?
No... not really. It's just... it's all been the same, mostly. I haven't felt better.
During these two years when you've been feeling this way, have you ever had thoughts about harming yourself or wishing you were dead?
No. I... I haven't. I just... I don't think about that.

You mentioned these feelings have been going on for about two years since you started college. During this entire two-year period, would you say you've felt this way pretty much every day, or have there been days or weeks where your mood and energy were noticeably better?
Just... every day, I guess. I don't really have better weeks. It just... stays the same.
Have you ever had a period of several days or more when you felt unusually happy, confident, or like you could do a lot of things, even if people around you thought it was excessive?
No... I haven't. I don't really... get happy like that. I just... I don't have that kind of energy.
During these two years, have you ever had a time when you felt more talkative than usual, or when your thoughts seemed to race, or when you had racing thoughts that were hard to keep up with?
No... not really. I don't... my thoughts don't race. I just... I don't talk much. It's always just... quiet, I guess.
